title: ingress-traffic-shield-terraform-module: unified internal NLB/ALB with TLS termination modes and robust health probes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a new Terraform module (ingress-traffic-shield) that consolidates internal load-balancing patterns for Private/VPC deployments. The module must support two primary modes: 1) ALB-terminated TLS with path/host routing and health-checked target groups, and 2) NLB passthrough (TLS forwarded) for customer-managed termination. It should expose toggles for TLS termination mode, ACM certificate ARNs, internal-only ALB/NLB creation, target group health-check translation (to reduce noisy failovers), and stable naming/tagging for downstream automation. This ticket covers design decisions, module API, implementation, integration tests in staging, and a phased rollout plan for existing Private customers to adopt the module.
acceptance_criteria: Module is published to our private Terraform registry with semantic versioning and example usage
Creates internal ALB/NLB with tags and predictable names; outputs ARNs/IDs for downstream stacks
Allows either ACM certificate ARN input or boolean use_self_signed for test environments
Health-check translator maps app-level readiness endpoints to AWS health check settings and exposes adjustable thresholds
Includes automated smoke test in staging that verifies routing, TLS behavior, and health-check-driven failover
CloudWatch metrics and alarm hooks are configured via module inputs (alarm_topic_arn, cpu/network thresholds)
Migration doc exists with step-by-step cutover to avoid connection drops for private customers
design_decisions: Default to ALB termination (alb_terminate) because it enables path-based routing, WAF integration later, and simpler cert lifecycle management
Provide nlb_passthrough for low-latency, L4 passthrough use-cases where customers insist on managing certs inside their network

Implement a health-check translator that converts application-level readiness (/ready or /healthz) into target group-compatible probes with configurable success_threshold/failure_threshold to reduce flapping seen under bursty traffic
Module will not create IAM roles or KMS keys; those are expected from infra baseline—keep module focused on networking resources
Use provider-agnostic variable names but implement AWS-specific resources (ALB/NLB/TargetGroups/Listeners) for private-deployments initiative
implementation_notes: Outputs: alb_arn, nlb_arn, primary_listener_arn, target_group_arns (list), dns_names (list)
Naming convention: <env>-<team>-ingress-<component> to maintain predictable stack names for SPF and support runbooks
Health-check translator accepts: path, port, interval, timeout, healthy_threshold, unhealthy_threshold, matcher_status
Expose a boolean 'enable_internal_alb' and 'enable_internal_nlb' but validate mutual exclusivity at plan time (only one default active)
Include acceptance/neg tests in ci/terraform/test/ that run against a sandbox AWS account and tear down resources after validation
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module and publish v0.1.0 to private registry (staging only)
2) Deploy example stacks in staging and run synthetic traffic tests for 72 hours
3) Reach out to 2 early adopters on Dedicated/Private to run a migration test (non-peak window)
4) Provide a migration runbook: create new ingress stack, register targets, monitor connection metrics for 30m, switch DNS to new ALB/NLB, decommission old stack after 2 hours stable
5) After two successful migrations, cut a release and update docs in Confluence/Docs site
testing_plan: Terraform plan/apply in sandbox VPC with sample Go HTTP app and readiness endpoints
Smoke tests: curl over TLS to ALB hostname (when alb_terminate) and verify certificate chain and HTTP2
For NLB passthrough: verify TCP handshake to backend pod and that backend presents expected cert
Health-check fuzzing: simulate application startup/shutdown to validate translator thresholds and avoid false-positive traffic rebalancing
Monitoring validation: create CloudWatch alarms via module inputs and assert SNS notification on simulated alarm
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misconfiguration causes customer outage during cutover. Mitigation: require staging migration and runbook + set low-traffic canary windows
Risk: Health check thresholds too strict cause flapping. Mitigation: conservative defaults (healthy_threshold=3, unhealthy_threshold=5) and allow overrides
Risk: Certificate automation mismatch for ALB termination. Mitigation: accept explicit ACM ARN and document ACM issuance steps or allow self-signed for tests
Risk: Naming collisions in shared VPCs. Mitigation: enforce tag and name prefix variables and validate uniqueness during plan
